Container.Name: NextDash
Container.DonateText: Find NextDash useful? Consider supporting the project.
Container.Overview:
NextDash is a lightweight, self-hosted bookmark dashboard that features a minimalist, keyboard-driven interface with extensive customization options, making it the perfect personal dashboard for power users. Based on the excellent ThinkDashboard.
Key features: • Keyboard-driven navigation for fast access to all your bookmarks • Extensive theme and layout customization • Inbox to collect new links fast: triage them, or keep them on a Kept tab and file whole groups later • Health view that finds broken, stale and duplicate links, with uptime monitoring and downtime alerts • Video bookmarks marked in the list, and played in the hover card without leaving the dashboard • Widgets beside your bookmarks: 21 built-in kinds (uptime, feeds, weather, calendar, disks, containers and more) plus a Custom widget for any JSON API • Six interface languages: English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish and Chinese • Lightweight and fast, no heavy dependencies • Actively maintained with regular releases
Links: • Website: https://www.nextdash.cc • Source code and releases: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash • Changelog: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash/releases • Devlog / release updates: https://www.nextdash.cc/news • Also available on GHCR: ghcr.io/jordibrouwer/nextdash:latest • User manual: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash/blob/main/MANUAL.md
The host widgets (Processor, Memory, Disks, Containers) are off until you fill in the optional paths and variables below — they are hidden under Show more settings. Section 11.4 of the manual explains what each one reads.
Support: open an issue on GitHub via the Support link above. Bug reports and feature requests are welcome.
Container.Changes:
### v1.15.7 (2026-09-30) - Bookmarks view: tick rows and a selection bar offers Edit, Re-check, Mute alerts, Export CSV and Delete - Containers: the tour covers the v1.15.6 features and runs once more - Containers: a stopped container is updated and left stopped; a rollback starts the old version; a VPN client can be updated - Dashboard: moving or undoing across pages no longer loses bookmarks, and Other is at the end of the page again - Inbox: the selection bar's Delete works, and an import stops at a full inbox instead of pushing out older links - Write token: settings no longer return stored keys and tokens, and the server log needs the token - More than a hundred smaller fixes across Health, Search, Config, widgets and feeds
### v1.15.6 (2026-09-30) - Containers: update automatically per container in a nightly window, rolled back if it stops, restarts or turns unhealthy - Containers: a web UI's bookmark shows its health after the link; click it to open the bookmark - Containers: a notice when a container stays above a CPU or memory line (90 % for 10 minutes by default) - Containers: choose the columns, sort by size or restarts, group by network or image, network and disk I/O in Resources - Disk: remove stopped containers in one go, and measure a bind mount's folder (Unraid appdata) on request - Fixed: followed container logs stayed empty in the browser until 4 KB had piled up
### v1.15.5 (2026-09-30) - Containers: a Size column with what each container wrote, measured in the background every half hour - Containers: tick several and start, stop, restart, update, remove or mute them at once; Backspace removes, running ones are stopped first after asking - Containers: a waiting update is an arrow before the name; names and images stay on one line, and three ports show before +N - Containers: Disk lists bind mounts, the appdata folders containers keep their data in, with who mounts each where - Config: the Docker host address is checked as you type, with an example; until it is set the view says where port links go
### v1.15.0 (2026-09-28) - Bookmarks view: the whole collection with health filters, grouping and a side panel for details, health and usage; the Health view lives here now - Containers view: the Docker host nextDash runs on, with status, ports, web UI links, logs, an hour of CPU and memory, and update checks - Containers: start, stop, restart and update from the view when NEXTDASH_DOCKER_CONTROL=1; nextDash never stops its own container - Inbox: one-line rows and a side panel; triage and Work through start from a pile and say why each item is there - Widgets: a Container list widget; Statistics rebuilt in five tabs with a Needs attention list - Themes: 34 new families, each light and dark (310 themes); a fresh install starts on Matrix Bluepill - Setup: Docker actions and Run as root are off by default; see the README for the socket and when root is needed
### v1.13.7 (2026-09-25) - Bookmark form: one column that reads the page once the address is in — icon, a name, its own line and picture, and suggested tags - Bookmark form: page and category are one field with a filter, and a new page or category can be made on the spot - Bookmark form: asks before saving without a category, names a link you already saved, and works by keyboard alone - Tags: suggested tags in Shift+T, the Config → Bookmarks side panel and the Tags button of a selection - Dashboard: a narrow window keeps as many columns as fit; only a phone held upright shows one - Fixed: page titles showed codes like & for an ampersand, and early clicks could not open the bookmark form

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the NextDash web interface

Config.Name: AppData
Config.Description: Persistent storage path for NextDash data (bookmarks, settings)

Config.Name: Write token
Config.Description: Optional. Require this token in the X-NextDash-Token header on every write. Leave empty for an open instance on a trusted network.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Optional. Addresses and CIDR ranges whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed, comma-separated — set this if nextDash sits behind a reverse proxy, so rate limits count per visitor instead of per proxy. Left empty the header is ignored.

Config.Name: Host proc
Config.Description: Optional. Mount the host /proc here for the Processor and Memory widgets. Host path: /proc

Config.Name: Host proc variable
Config.Description: Optional. Set to /host/proc once the mount above is filled in.

Config.Name: Host disks
Config.Description: Optional. Mount the array here for the Disks widget. Host path: /mnt — then name /mnt/user or /mnt/cache in the widget.

Config.Name: Host root variable
Config.Description: Optional. Set to /host/root once the disks mount above is filled in.

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: Optional. Mount the Docker socket here for the Containers widget. Host path: /var/run/docker.sock — read-only still exposes the daemon's whole read API, so use a socket proxy if that is too much.

Config.Name: Docker socket variable
Config.Description: Optional. Set to /var/run/docker.sock once the socket mount above is filled in. Unset, the Containers widget is hidden.

Config.Name: Docker actions
Config.Description: Optional. 1 lets the Containers view start, stop, update and remove containers; 0 keeps it read-only. A writable socket is root on the host, so set a write token as well.

Config.Name: Run as root
Config.Description: Optional. 1 keeps nextDash running as root, needed only when the Docker socket belongs to root's group (gid 0). Unraid's socket belongs to the docker group (gid 281), so leave this at 0 here.
